**What I found:** Don't build the plugin subsystem; drop it (the record calls this DROP). JSON is the only format in the code, and you said nobody has asked for another, so a registry would be a plugin interface with only one plugin.

**Why it matters:** Once third parties write plugins against the PluginRegistry, its API is public and hard to change, and today it would hold only `toJson`. If you skip it, nothing breaks: adding a second format later means one new file and one flag.

**Do this first:**
1. Make no changes to `src/`, and record the decision as a closed issue so the idea isn't proposed again without new evidence (this isn't a git repo, so there's no commit history to hold it).
2. When someone asks for a specific format, add `src/format/<name>.js` and a `--format` lookup in `src/cli.js:6-9`. Only add a registry when a third format or an actual external plugin author shows up.

**What I did not check:**
- I relied on your statement that nobody has asked for another format. I didn't search an issue tracker; searching it for "format", "csv" or "yaml" would confirm it.

```
Subject:        PluginRegistry subsystem for third-party output formats
Mode:           Prospective
Necessity:      Fail
Necessity note: Generality without instantiation (§1a). A plugin interface would have one implementation
                (toJson, src/format/json.js:1). No second format and no third-party plugin author exists.
                Alchemy core directive 2 says to name the second concrete instance before writing an
                abstraction, and none can be named.
Outcome evidence: none
Decision:       DROP
Rationale:      The problem the registry solves (varying output formats from third parties) doesn't happen
                in this codebase. Today each command calls toJson directly, which is 3 simple edges. A
                registry adds a new kind of module, a longer call chain, and a public plugin contract
                (§8b one-way door), all with nothing to justify them.
Next action:    Stop. Leave the code unchanged and record the rejection in the issue tracker.
Verification:   Read all 3 callers of toJson; confirmed json.js is the only formatter
Minimal alt:    On the first concrete request: add src/format/<name>.js and a `formats` map with a
                --format flag in src/cli.js. Build no registry until a third format or a real external
                plugin author exists.
Revisit when:   A user or customer files a request that names a specific non-JSON format, or an external
                party asks to ship their own formatter.
```
